Description: Customization is a key aspect of the OFBiz (Open For Business) platform, providing businesses with a robust and adaptable base to customize their enterprise software solutions according to their unique operational requirements. The *Menus.xml file of a component, essential for designing user interfaces that are both intuitive and tailored to the specific roles and tasks of its users, plays a significant role in this context, as referenced within screen widgets and Freemarker templates. However, as customizations and the project's source code evolve over time, the likelihood of encountering merge conflicts increases significantly, especially when attempting to incorporate customizations alongside ongoing bug fixes and enhancements from the project. To improve the appeal of OFbiz and the developer experience, it is recommended to shift from fixed menu locations to a parameterized approach in our components and plugins. This change would enable developers to more seamlessly incorporate a 'custom' menu, facilitating the integration of project updates.
title: HumanRes - Move from hard-code menu location to parameterized

Description: Several parts of the framework and applications depend on the myportal plugin, so they break or degrade when it is not deployed. This removes those dependencies, as the first step towards retiring myportal (see the [retirement thread|https://lists.apache.org/thread/gsdtr4s6ry2g6v87k8t8xbjlvwhpyg73]). Portal pages and the portlets each application defines are not affected. h3. Dependencies * *Portlet permission services:* nine portlets (accounting 2, humanres 2, order 5) set {{securityServiceName}} to {{portalPermissionIsEmployee}} or {{portalPermissionIsCustomer}}, which only myportal defines, together with the {{MYPORTAL_EMPLOYEE}} and {{MYPORTAL_CUSTOMER}} permissions they check. Without myportal, {{ListPortalPortlets.groovy}} fails when it calls the missing service, so the list of portlets to add to a portal page cannot be shown. * *Portlet reordering:* {{common-theme/js/plugins/myportal.js}} posts to {{/myportal/control/updatePortalPagePortletSeqAjax}}, although the request is defined in the framework's {{portal-controller.xml}}. Reordering portlets in the sfa, catalog, webtools or example portal pages therefore only works when myportal is deployed. It should post to the current webapp. * *Order emails:* the create, completed and added-note customer request notifications link to {{/myportal/control/showPortletMainDecorator}}. They should link to the request view in the webapp of the store's web site. * *Labels:* order forms and screens use eleven {{MyPortal*}} labels that only {{MyPortalUiLabels.xml}} defines, and {{OrderViewScreens.xml}} loads that file directly. The labels in use should move into the order labels. {{MyPortalCustRequestNotificationMailCreation}} in {{PartyScreens.xml}} is defined nowhere, so that screen title shows the raw key. * *Portal page admin permission:* {{PortalPageServices.groovy}} lets {{MYPORTALBASE_ADMIN}} edit any portal page, but only myportal seeds that permission. It should be seeded with the portal page entities in common.
title: Remove core dependencies on the myportal plugin
